subject.title: fix(exec): stop isolated state dirs from moving live approvals

question: Should bare `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` relocation permanently lose the documented direct-doctor approval import, or should OpenClaw retain an explicit non-destructive operator migration mechanism?
rationale: The patch strengthens state isolation but intentionally removes a shipped upgrade workflow and changes the resulting default approval posture; repository evidence cannot choose that compatibility policy without owner intent.

options.title: Retain explicit import
options.body: Forbid ambient and automatic cross-state access while preserving a deliberate copy-only import with focused fresh-install and upgrade proof.

options.title: Retire the migration
options.body: Accept unconditional isolation only with explicit owner approval and release-facing guidance for users moving an existing primary state root.

recommendation.title: Retain explicit import
recommendation.body: Forbid ambient and automatic cross-state access while preserving a deliberate copy-only import with focused fresh-install and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history connects this contributor directly to the approval relocation capability and its isolation follow-ups.
